children: Microsoft (MSFT) is facing scrutiny over how it justifies its AI infrastructure outlays, with investor Michael Burry (Trades, Portfolio) suggesting the spending race may be shaped as much by ambitions for market control as by customers' immediate needs, according to a Thursday post on his Substack.

Burry's concern centers on the incentives behind the industry's data-center buildout. He argues executives may use financial measures to support their plans while analysts have not adequately challenged the case for such large commitments. In his view, companies are acting on an expectation that a handful of providers will dominate AI and cloud services.

That framework also raises questions about spending by OpenAI, Anthropic and Oracle (ORCL). Burry argues these businesses may be investing not to displace established leaders but to secure places in the same concentrated market.

He identifies Microsoft, Amazon (AMZN), Google parent Alphabet (GOOG) and Meta Platforms (META) as companies whose positions would be difficult to dislodge in their respective markets. Apple (AAPL) has been an exception to his broader criticism of technology spending. His comments shift attention to whether projected returns justify the industry's expanding AI infrastructure budgets.

title: Michael Burry Issues Fresh Warning on Microsoft AI Spending
